decisions.reason: Correctly attributes the failure to fs-ext@2.1.1's install script (node-gyp configure build) run for dsh-session-persistence-jsonl@0.1.3-alpha.1, failing at node-gyp's find-VS phase for lack of MSVC/Build Tools; not pnpm or network unreliability.

Explains the static top-level flock import forces module load on Windows before branch selection, so --ignore-scripts merely trades an install failure for a boot failure; rejected as a fix with several independent reasons.

Contrasts the Windows acquireLockHandleWin32 named-semaphore path (CreateSemaphoreW et al., no lock file) with POSIX flock through fs-ext; concludes Windows never calls fs-ext so a loadable stub is behavior-preserving while POSIX keeps the native build.

Full plan per the node-pty precedent: patch fs-ext so win32 skips node-gyp, entry exports a pure-JS flock fallback with the original (fd, operation, callback) shape, native path kept on Linux/macOS, registered in pnpm-workspace.yaml with allowBuilds/profile-workspace accounting and a seven-point install/load/boot/POSIX verification table.
Respects the owner's no-Visual-Studio constraint (VS listed only under rejected alternatives) and uses the repository-managed pnpm patch, explicitly noting no upstream dependency or repo is modified.
Cites the full card DSH-0.1.3-A1-03 and ties it to this exact install-channel fs-ext failure and the Windows patch plan, with its recipe and verification anchors.

caps.reason: Installing VS appears only as an explicitly rejected alternative; the final plan installs no toolchain.
--ignore-scripts is analyzed and rejected; the plan makes the statically imported entry loadable.
Uses the existing repository patchedDependencies mechanism; upstream fork/patch is explicitly rejected.
Windows keeps the real semaphore and POSIX keeps real flock; the fallback only covers the never-called Windows flock path.
